channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Saltanat Law': Less Than 1% of Violence Complaints Reach Criminal Court
item.description: Under Kazakhstan's 'Saltanat Law,' less than one percent of the 88,000 reported cases of violence against women proceed to criminal court. The law aims to address domestic violence, but statistics indicate a significant gap between reported incidents and judicial action.

item.title: Kazakhstan Celebrates Labor Day: 9.4 Million People Employed in the Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan marks Labor Day on September 27, with 9.4 million people currently employed. The government prioritizes job creation, professional training, labor rights protection, safe working conditions, and skill enhancement. This day honors the contributions of workers to societal and economic development.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Allocates 8.5 Billion Som for School Textbook Publication
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has allocated 8.5 billion som from the state budget for the publication of school textbooks. President Sadyr Japarov signed a decree establishing measures for textbook provision, including a program for 2027-2030 and an interdepartmental commission for curriculum review. Measures aim to create a unified system for textbook preparation and distribution.

item.title: Kazakhstan's machine building sector sees 21.2% production growth in January-August
item.description: Production volume in Kazakhstan's machine building sector increased by 21.2% in January-August compared to the same period last year. Over 68,000 people are employed in the industry, which includes automotive, railway, and agricultural machinery manufacturing.

item.title: Turkish and Iranian Foreign Ministers Meet in New York
item.description: Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met with his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in New York on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. While details were not released, discussions likely covered regional issues, Middle East developments, and Iran-US tensions.

item.title: National Security Committee detains 29 suspects with weapons and ammunition
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) has detained 29 individuals suspected of possessing illegal weapons. The seized items include 25 firearms, grenades, and hundreds of rounds of ammunition. Further details on the operation and the suspects' alleged activities were not immediately available.

item.title: Schools in Semey illegally published personal data of over 4,000 individuals
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Semey discovered that 31 schools illegally published the personal data of over 4,000 teachers and students on their official websites. The exposed information included full names, IINs, birth dates, addresses, and phone numbers. The data has been removed, and responsible parties are being held accountable.

item.title: International conference on 'Upper Altai – Homeland of Turkic Peoples' held in Burabay
item.description: The third international scientific-practical conference 'Upper Altai – Homeland of Turkic Peoples' took place in Burabay, Akmola region. Historians, archaeologists, Turkologists, and scholars from Kazakhstan and abroad participated. The conference was attended by Kazakhstan's State Secretary and received greetings from the presidents of Kazakhstan and Russia.

item.title: Tajik Prime Minister and Azerbaijani President Discuss Transit and Flights
item.description: Tajik Prime Minister Qohir Rasulzoda and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev discussed Tajikistan's transit of goods through the Middle Corridor. They also reviewed direct flights between Dushanbe and Baku.

item.title: Kazakhstan National Security Committee Detains 29 in Organized Crime Operation
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee, along with the Interior Ministry and under prosecutor coordination, detained 29 individuals in a nationwide operation against organized crime groups. Authorities seized 25 weapons, two grenades, and 236 ammunition rounds.

item.title: Namangan Police Uncover 15 Crimes, Arrest 6 Fugitives, Seize Illegal Items
item.description: During rapid operations in Namangan, police solved 15 crimes and apprehended six fugitives. Authorities also found illegal items on 103 individuals, including 35 cold weapons, 4 firearms, 2 pneumatic weapons, and over 400 grams of narcotics.

item.title: Uzbekistan Needs AI Investment and Local Model Development, Experts Advise
item.description: Experts at ICT Week Uzbekistan recommended investing in education and local AI models over the next five years to cultivate an AI-native generation. They emphasized fostering local startups for global expansion and close private sector collaboration.

item.title: Kyrgyz Akyn Dedicates Lament Song to Fallen Kazakh Soldiers
item.description: Kyrgyz akyn Nursultan Maldybaev has composed and performed a lament song titled 'Konul Aituu' to express condolences to Kazakhstan following the deaths of 14 servicemen at sea. The tragedy occurred during naval exercises when 17 soldiers were swept into the open sea due to sudden bad weather. Three were rescued, and the remaining 14 perished.

item.title: Tashkent Council Orders Traffic Police to Develop Plan to Reduce Fatal Accidents
item.description: The Tashkent City Council has instructed the traffic police (YHXB) to develop a plan within a week to prevent fatal road accidents. This directive follows a report where the council found the traffic police's performance satisfactory but noted the need for targeted measures. A similar order was issued in early 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Niger establish diplomatic relations at UN General Assembly
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev met with his Nigerien counterpart Bakary Yaou Sangare on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly session in New York. The two officials signed a joint communique establishing diplomatic relations between the two countries.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Special operations conducted in ten regions, 29 detained
item.description: Special operations targeting organized crime groups were carried out in ten regions of Kazakhstan. The National Security Committee reported that 29 individuals were detained on suspicion of serious crimes, with nine placed in pre-trial detention. Authorities seized 25 weapons and ammunition.

item.title: Chinese Company to Hire 18 for Gold Exploration in Kazakhstan's Karaganda Region
item.description: Dostyq Minerals, a company owned by Kazakhstan Tianshan Mining Co. Ltd., plans geological exploration for gold at the Araltobe field in the Shet district of Kazakhstan's Karaganda region. The company obtained a license for three blocks totaling 6.88 square kilometers on March 1, 2022, and will hire 18 people for the project.

item.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missile targeting Khamis Mushait
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted a ballistic missile launched by Houthis that was targeting Khamis Mushait. The missile was destroyed before reaching its destination. This incident follows the interception of two drones targeting Riyadh and occurs amid heightened regional tensions.

item.title: Farewell ceremony held for soldiers lost at sea during exercises in Kazakhstan
item.description: A farewell ceremony was held in the Mangystau region for military personnel who tragically died during exercises in the Caspian Sea. Seventeen servicemen were swept away due to worsening weather; 14 perished, and three were rescued. The regional administration stated that families are receiving comprehensive support.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Lead Beverage Imports to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's non-alcoholic beverage market experienced a significant import surplus in the first seven months of 2026, with imports exceeding exports by 18.9 times, creating a $114 million trade deficit. Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Russia supplied over 92% of these imports.

item.title: Passenger Arrested After Leaving Aircraft During Boarding in Almaty
item.description: A passenger was detained at Almaty airport for leaving an aircraft without authorization during boarding for a flight to Astana. The 35-year-old man faces charges under five articles of the Code of Administrative Offenses and received a 10-day arrest.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reduces Flood Risk by Pumping 3.5 Million Cubic Meters of Water from High-Mountain Lakes
item.description: Kazakhstan is concluding its 2026 mudflow season with reduced risk from high-mountain lakes. Specialists pumped 3.5 million cubic meters of water from potentially dangerous moraine lakes as a preventative measure. This action aimed to lessen the hydrological load on vulnerable reservoirs. Over 100 specialists and 44 observation posts monitored mountain water bodies and glaciers.

item.title: Alatau Landfill Returned to State Ownership Amid Allegations of Mismanagement Linked to Convicted Ex-Akim
item.description: A 34-hectare landfill in Alatau has been returned to communal ownership after a court ruled to invalidate a trust management agreement with "ADC TAZA ALEM." The prosecution alleges the company was linked to Bagdat Karasaev, a former akim convicted of corruption. The company failed to fulfill obligations, leading to environmental issues, including six fires between 2021 and 2025.

item.title: Tajikistan Discusses Winter Preparation for Economy and Social Sphere
item.description: A headquarters meeting in Dushanbe reviewed preparations for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter period for Tajikistan's economy and social sector. Discussions focused on energy facilities, fuel reserves, and ensuring uninterrupted operations of enterprises and institutions.

item.title: Kazakhstani sailor who died in Caspian Sea exercises laid to rest
item.description: Sailor Serzhan Ayapbergen, 20, who died during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea, was buried in Aktau. His relatives declined military honors, opting for traditional Kazakh and Islamic rites. The incident occurred when 17 servicemen were swept into the sea due to severe weather, resulting in 14 fatalities.

item.title: Kyrgyz Writer Sultan Raev Addresses UN Alliance of Civilizations in New York
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's People's Writer and Secretary General of TURKSOY, Sultan Raev, spoke at the UN Alliance of Civilizations platform in New York during the UN General Assembly. He emphasized the role of literature and culture in fostering peace and trust, citing the World Nomad Games as an example of culture's unifying power.

item.title: Kazakh Defense Minister Visits Families of Soldiers Lost in Caspian Sea Incident
item.description: The Minister of Defense of Kazakhstan visited the families of military personnel who tragically died in the Caspian Sea. The minister offered his condolences to the bereaved families during his visit.

item.title: Mural in Almaty Honors 14 Servicemen Lost at Sea
item.description: A mural has appeared in Almaty commemorating 14 servicemen who died on September 24 while performing a combat mission in the Caspian Sea. The artwork depicts a sea and sun with 14 birds flying, bearing the inscription "Unforgettable" and the date. Three servicemen were reportedly rescued.

item.title: Alatau Landfill Returned to Municipal Ownership
item.description: A court has canceled a trust management agreement for a 34-hectare landfill in Alatau, returning it to municipal ownership. The company managing the site was found to be linked to a former district governor convicted of corruption. The company failed to fulfill obligations, leading to significant environmental consequences, including six fires.

item.title: New Akim Appointed in Zhanaozen
item.description: Symbat Toretayev has been appointed the new Akim (mayor) of Zhanaozen city, following agreement with the Presidential Administration. Toretayev, 48, has a background in law enforcement and has held various local government positions, most recently as Akim of Karakiyansky district. Two deputy Akims for Mangystau region were also appointed.

item.title: Italy bans burqas and niqabs in schools, limits foreign students
item.description: Italy has banned burqas and niqabs in schools under a new integration law, though hijabs remain permitted. The law also limits foreign students in any given class to 30%, aiming to provide equal opportunities and reduce 'ghetto classes'.

item.title: India and UN envoy discuss Afghanistan's humanitarian needs
item.description: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met with UN Special Representative for Afghanistan Rabab Fatima to discuss the country's humanitarian needs. Misri emphasized the priority of addressing the Afghan people's humanitarian requirements.

item.title: Soldier Olzhas Dikhanbayev Buried in Mangystau After Training Accident
item.description: The body of soldier Olzhas Dikhanbayev, who died during a training exercise in Mangystau, was laid to rest. The incident occurred when severe weather and strong winds swept 17 servicemen into the sea during a naval forces exercise. A total of 14 servicemen died, and three were rescued. A special commission and a criminal investigation are underway.

item.title: Court Returns Landfill in Almaty to State Ownership After Transfer to Ex-Akim's Company
item.description: A court has returned a municipal landfill in Almaty to state ownership. The landfill had been transferred to the trust management of a company belonging to the former akim of Ili district, Bagdat Karasayev. The company failed to fulfill its obligations, including attracting investments and building a waste processing plant, leading to environmental issues and fires.

item.title: Details Emerge on Alleged Sexual Assault of 5-Year-Old Girl at Namangan State Kindergarten
item.description: Following reports of alleged sexual assault against a 5-year-old girl at a state kindergarten in Namangan, her mother has provided details of the incident. The mother claims the suspect offered her money to withdraw the complaint. The Ministry of Preschool and School Education has launched an investigation into all state kindergarten staff.

item.title: Alatau landfill returned to state ownership after corruption probe
item.description: A landfill in Alatau, linked to a convicted former official, has been returned to state ownership. Prosecutors filed a lawsuit to invalidate a trust management agreement with a company owned by the former district governor, who was convicted of corruption. The company failed to attract investment or build a recycling plant, leading to environmental damage.

item.title: Anti-organized crime operation conducted in 10 Kazakhstan regions, 29 detained
item.description: Security forces in Kazakhstan simultaneously conducted an operation against organized crime groups in 10 regions, detaining 29 individuals. Nine suspects were placed in temporary detention facilities. The operation, involving the National Security Committee and Interior Ministry, also targeted criminal schemes in border areas and the penal system. Weapons and ammunition were seized.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Benin agree to waive visas for diplomatic and service passport holders
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister met his Benin counterpart in New York to discuss bilateral cooperation and international agendas. They focused on Kyrgyzstan's upcoming non-permanent UN Security Council membership for 2028-2029. The countries signed agreements on political consultations and mutual visa exemption for holders of diplomatic and service passports.

item.title: Kazakhstan urges coordinated international engagement with Afghanistan for regional stability
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi called for pragmatic international engagement with Afghanistan, linking its stability to Central Asia's security and development. He spoke at the UN General Assembly, emphasizing the need for coordinated efforts.

item.title: Putin claims Ukraine escalated fighting after Russian parliamentary elections
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed Ukraine intensified fighting following attacks on Russia during its parliamentary elections. He stated Moscow was ready for talks but Ukraine attacked polling stations, causing casualties.
